observations: Photo 0: a metal transmission/gearbox unit lying on wet pavement amid other disassembled engine/transmission parts, in a yard setting.
Photo 1: wider shot showing the same unit alongside several other gearboxes/engines in a junk-yard pile, with a person's leg visible.
Photo 2: close crop of the gearbox casing, same angle as photo 0.
All three photos carry a 'POSTED ON JIJI / GEARUP INC.' watermark, suggesting these may be stock/supplier catalog photos rather than photos of the specific unit for sale.
Casing shows hand-chalked marks ('CA', 'PR0') and a dab of green paint, but no stamped VIN, part number, or manufacturer tag is legible in any photo.
No badge, casting number, or label reading 'Jeep', 'Wrangler', '3.6L', or any transmission code is visible or readable in any photo.
Surface shows oxidation, grime, and disconnected wiring/hoses consistent with a pulled used part; no fluid, dipstick, or electrical test shown.

identity.kind: vehicle automatic transmission/gearbox assembly (seller claims Jeep Wrangler 3.6L, 2011-2017, 4x4)

claims.evidence: No part tag, casting number, or badge legible in photo 0, 1, or 2 to confirm make/model/engine size.
No shipping, customs, or import documentation shown in any photo.
Conflicts with the 'Direct America drive' claim in the same listing; the two origin stories cannot both be true, and neither is shown in photos.
No test bench video, running clip, or diagnostic scan shown; photos are static and show an un-mounted, disconnected unit.
No odometer, service sticker, or seal/bolt-paint photo showing an unopened casing.

risks.risk: Actual make/model may not match the Jeep Wrangler 3.6L claim, which drives the entire price.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the stamped part number/casting tag on the transmission case or bell housing.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this — model sets the price range (from low-value small gearboxes to high-value V8/4x4 units).

risks.risk: Photos may be generic stock/catalog images (GEARUP INC watermark) rather than the actual unit being sold.
risks.proof: A fresh photo of the unit with today's date/newspaper or a handwritten note with the seller's name, taken at the yard.
risks.if_unproven: price as a generic used part of unconfirmed origin, not the specific advertised unit.

risks.risk: Internal wear, mechatronic/solenoid failure, or fluid contamination not visible from outside.
risks.proof: Video of the transmission being bench-tested or installed and shifting through gears, plus a fluid-color photo.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for-parts condition.

risks.risk: Casing may have been opened/rebuilt despite 'never opened' claim.
risks.proof: Close-up of factory-seal bolts/paint marks on the case seams.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly opened/rebuilt, not factory-sealed.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the stamped part/casting number on the transmission housing or bell housing.
A fresh, dated photo or video of the actual unit (not a catalog/stock image) at the seller's current location.
A video of the gearbox being bench-tested or shifted through gears.
Close-up of case seam bolts/paint to show it has not been opened.
response.reason: The photos show an unlabeled gearbox with no readable part number, tag, or model marking, and the only identity claim (Jeep Wrangler 3.6L) comes solely from the seller's text, which conflicts internally (America vs Belgium origin); since the model is what sets the price among the comparables, no worst-case price can be assigned until the identifying tag or a dated proof-of-item photo is provided.
